items.title: Putter Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 27, 2024
items.q: And he was a very good bass player. His son was out here for a while, Duffy. Very good drummer. Very good drummer. I think he ended up in Miami. But Chubby was a very good bass player.

ctx.x: thought of him back then watching Woody Herman’s band with the lack of amplification and he said, “A lot of times your arms and fingers get numb. You’re playing — you start to shake physically at the moment, and then someone looks at you and says ‘take one’ the laugh of the century, somebody points to the bass player after 28 choruses, your hands are like this. My hands were so ugly I used to keep them in my pocket all the time.”

Yeah. Absolutely. And he was playing without an amp. And he was a very good bass player. His son was out here for a while, Duffy. Very good drummer. Very good drummer. I think he ended up in Miami. But Chubby was a very good bass player.
Well with a song like that, at that tempo, I’m trying to form a question here — how many of your notes would you not play if you were playing at a civilized tempo?
